title: PIVOT- Input-aware Path Selection for Energy-efficient ViT Inference
problem: Attention modules in vision transformers perform intricate spatial correlations that significantly impact accuracy and latency. The challenge is to modulate the number of attention operations according to input feature complexity for optimal delay-accuracy tradeoffs.
motivation: Energy-efficient ViT inference is critical for practical deployment in resource-constrained environments and edge devices.
method: PIVOT employs a co-optimization framework that dynamically skips attention operations based on input difficulty assessment. It uses hardware-in-loop co-search to determine optimal attention skip configurations. The approach is evaluated on ZCU102 MPSoC FPGA, achieving significant energy savings through selective attention computation.
key_novelty: Input-aware dynamic attention path selection using hardware-in-loop co-search to discover optimal skip configurations for energy-efficient ViT inference.
contributions: Co-optimization framework (PIVOT) for input-aware selective attention skipping in vision transformers
Hardware-in-loop co-search methodology for determining optimal attention skip configurations
Demonstrates 2.7× lower energy-delay product (EDP) on FPGA with only 0.2% accuracy reduction
Achieves 1.3% higher accuracy and 1.8× better throughput than prior works on CPUs and GPUs

metrics.accuracy: 0.2% reduction vs LVViT-S, 1.3% higher than prior work
